title: Valentine single-page prompt with evasive No and Yes celebration meme

requirements.summary: Build a single-page romantic Valentine prompt with exactly two choices (Yes/No) using a pink-and-white theme and iPad-friendly layout.
acceptanceCriteria: Landing view shows one clear question: "Will you be my Valentine?"
Exactly two visible choices are present: a "Yes" button and a "No" button
Overall styling uses a coherent pink-and-white romantic theme (background, typography, button styles)
The page works in Chrome on iPad-sized screens without layout overflow or clipped controls

file_operations.description: Create the single-page UI layout with the question text and exactly two prominent buttons (Yes/No), using a responsive container that avoids overflow/clipping on iPad-sized screens.
Add global pink-and-white romantic theme styling (background, typography, button baseline styles) using existing global styling entry points; ensure good contrast and responsive spacing.

requirements.summary: Make the No button evasive on hover (desktop) and touch/pointer interaction (iPad) while keeping it visible and keeping Yes stable/clickable.
acceptanceCriteria: On desktop: moving the cursor over the "No" button causes it to reposition before a click can occur
On touch devices (e.g., iPad Chrome): attempting to tap/press the "No" button causes it to reposition, making it effectively unclickable
The "No" button remains visible on-screen after moving (does not move off-canvas)
The "Yes" button remains stable and clickable throughout

file_operations.description: Implement reusable evasive-position logic that computes a new safe position within a measured container/viewport on hover and pointer/touch interaction, clamping so the button stays fully visible.
Wire the evasive No behavior into the No button using hover and pointer/touch handlers (e.g., pointerenter/pointerdown/touchstart) while keeping the Yes button position stable and always clickable.

requirements.summary: On Yes click, transition to a celebration state showing the meme image and the exact text "Good choice".
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking "Yes" reliably switches the view/state to a celebration screen (or modal)
The celebration view displays the exact text: "Good choice"
The celebration view displays the provided/generated meme image (served as a static frontend asset)
The initial question and buttons are no longer the primary focus once "Yes" is clicked (hidden or clearly de-emphasized)

file_operations.description: Add UI state handling so clicking Yes transitions to a celebration view that prominently renders the exact text "Good choice" and displays the meme image; de-emphasize or replace the initial prompt/buttons.

requirements.summary: Add and render the required static meme image asset from the frontend public folder (no backend involvement).
acceptanceCriteria: All generated images are placed under frontend/public/assets/generated
The "Yes" success state renders the meme image from frontend/public/assets/generated via a static path
No backend changes are required for serving images

file_operations.description: Add the generated static meme image asset at frontend/public/assets/generated/valentine-good-choice-meme.dim_1024x1024.png so it can be served directly by the frontend build.

Reference and render the static image asset from frontend/public/assets/generated/valentine-good-choice-meme.dim_1024x1024.png in the Yes celebration state, ensuring it loads correctly in production builds.
